data.title: PMV Pharmaceuticals Reports 48% Response Rate in Ovarian Cancer Trial; NDA Planned for Q1 2027
data.description:
PMV Pharmaceuticals reported updated Phase 2 results for rezatapopt, showing a 48% response rate in platinum-resistant or refractory ovarian cancer and an NDA submission planned for the first quarter of 2027.

Key Highlights:

  • Among 65 ovarian cancer patients, confirmed ORR was 48%, with a median response duration of 10.4 months.
  • Across 168 evaluable patients in all cohorts, ORR was 36%, with a median response duration of 8.1 months.
  • Rezatapopt responses were reported across eight tumor types with TP53 Y220C-mutated, KRAS wild-type tumors.
  • Most treatment-related adverse events were Grade 1 or 2; individual Grade 3 event rates were no higher than 7.2%.
  • PMV plans to submit an NDA for platinum-resistant or refractory ovarian cancer in the first quarter of 2027.

Original SEC Filing: PMV Pharmaceuticals, Inc. [ PMVP ] - 8-K - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: Automakers sue NJ over vehicle warranty and recall repair law - Reuters
data.description:
Ford , Honda , Volkswagen , and Stellantis’ FCA unit  are suing New Jersey in an attempt to block a 7-month-old law that leaves automakers responsible for warranty and recall costs.

According to Reuters, the automakers claim the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act gives franchised dealerships “unilateral and unchecked power” to charge “extortionate” prices for repairs that automakers are responsible for.  Manufacturers also argue that the statute prevents them from avoiding or recovering the added costs.

The New Jersey Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act requires automakers to pay dealers at least 1.5% of a used vehicle’s value per month if recall parts are unavailable within 30 days of a stop-sale or do-not-drive notice until parts arrive or the vehicle is sold.

The law also sets rules for how automakers reimburse dealers for warranty and recall repairs, including labor rates, prices for parts, labor hours, and claim processing.

If the automakers are successful in their challenge, it would limit the reach of the current payment system for dealerships in the state. If the challenge fails, the plaintiffs claim the law gives dealers too much control over repair reimbursement.

data.title: Nasdaq plunges 5% a day after Anthropic debut, but investors still believe in AI
data.description:
Tech stocks slumped on Friday to a 10% weekly decline in the Nasdaq composite , the biggest since 2020, just surpassing the pullback in response to the Liberation Day tariff announcements in spring 2025.

Nvidia tumbled 14% on Friday and 23% for the week after Reuters reported the Securities and Exchange Commission was probing its accounting. Anthropic dropped 9% after earlier falling as much as 14% following its blockbuster IPO, and the semiconductor index of AI favorites fell 11% in a broad retreat from risk.

For the day, the Nasdaq dropped 5.3%, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX fell 3.7% and Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX volatility index, soared 33% to 37. The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note fell 12 basis points to 4.93%.

Even so, investors largely said they continued to believe in the AI trade, which took markets to record highs as recently as last month.

COMMENTS:

MICHAEL MONAGHAN, PORTFOLIO MANAGER AND PARTNER AT FOUNDER ETFS, DALLAS, TEXAS:

"In the short run, sentiment drives prices. In the long run, fundamentals do. Right now the market is selling first and asking questions later. In our view, the fundamentals remain strong, and we expect prices to reflect them over time."

GENE GOLDMAN, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT CETERA, EL SEGUNDO, CA:

"This week’s chip earnings were an earnings test, and they passed it. Yesterday’s AI IPO is a valuation test, and with the 10-year around 5% and the Fed still hiking, investors are asking how much of the AI story is already priced in."

RICHARD SAPERSTEIN, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, TREASURY PARTNERS, NEW YORK:

"The stock market is going through an AI repricing, reflecting an environment of slowing data center buildouts, reduced funding sources for AI-related projects and a slower trajectory of technology-related earnings growth. This has been exacerbated by the Nvidia crisis and the Democratic midterm win, which were a one-two punch for the AI story.

"Investors are broadly reducing exposure to technology and AI-related equities in favor of non-technology sectors, such as health care, energy and utilities.

"Within technology, we still like the hyperscalers, which can benefit from any slowing data center buildouts since they already own many of them, and cybersecurity, as the recent wave of cyber outages increases demand for their products.

"Investors should maintain long-term allocations to large cap technology stocks, as AI adoption will continue to accelerate and drive economic growth and productivity. A slowdown in AI spending will extend the cycle over a longer time period. In the near term, hyperscaler capital expenditures may begin to slow, giving rise to free cash flow."

MARK HACKETT, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST FROM NATIONWIDE FINANCIAL, DOWNINGTOWN, PENNSYLVANIA:

"The current environment is reminiscent of the market action surrounding Liberation Day and the breakout of the conflict with Iran. Those resolved quickly as the reality did not match the fear, with retail investors aggressively buying the dip and indexes returning to record highs within months.

"After months of rotational price action, the recent de-grossing feels as though it has arrived gradually, then suddenly. A capitulatory washout could ultimately prove constructive. If this evolves into a true flush, it may serve as the reset needed to improve positioning, sentiment, and the odds of a more sustainable rally into year-end. The fundamental backdrop remains strong, and sentiment and positioning are supportive from a contrarian standpoint, but picking bottoms is difficult when the market is so emotional."

TIM GHRISKEY, SENIOR PORTFOLIO STRATEGIST AT INGALLS & SNYDER IN NEW YORK:

"Interest rates are going up and we have signs of consumer inflation. The Fed is likely to raise rates at the December meeting and possibly the January meeting as well. Financial markets hate higher interest rates. It's medicine that's often necessary to break down inflation. A lot of the inflation is energy related, oil related, but, that finds its way into various other goods and services.

"In general, you know, we have an increasing interest rate environment. We have for a while, and the market sort of has been ignoring it somewhat but it's out there. Since mid-October when the slide began to happen there's been more awareness of it. Fed speakers have been talking about it more. We've had a lot of Fed speak, especially this week. That's the overriding issue.

"The other issue technology in general and AI. Some of that is valuation related and some is the disruption at Nvdia. It was the largest company in the US market and now it’s not. It's had this drama and currently a lack of leadership. It's clear to us that the CFO, who's the interim CEO, as well as keeping her CFO job and everything else, is probably a bit overwhelmed by all of this."

PHILIP PALUMBO, CEO AND CIO, PALUMBO WEALTH MANAGEMENT, NEW YORK:

"In the short term, markets move based on sentiment, emotion, headlines, and investors’ opinions about what may happen next. Fear and uncertainty can drive prices lower, sometimes very quickly.

"But over time, what matters most is the underlying value of the businesses we own. Their earnings, cash flow, competitive advantages, and ability to grow ultimately determine their long-term value. That is where our attention remains focused."

JIM AWAD, SENIOR MANAGING DIRECTOR AT CLEARSTEAD ADVISORS LLC IN NEW YORK:

"You have a growth fear in terms of the economy because of the wealth destruction in the stock market, because of fears of moderation in AI spending, and fears that Nvidia problems will spread beyond Nvidia. So you haven't yet seen a significant deceleration in profit estimates for next year. But that would naturally follow if this turbulence continues. But my expectation is that the turbulence will pass, stock prices will recover, and interest rates on balance will be higher over coming months."

LAWRENCE GILLUM, CHIEF FIXED INCOME STRATEGIST AT LPL FINANCIAL, FORT MILL, SOUTH CAROLINA:

"Right now, we think that this is just kind of more technical in nature and not necessarily something that is broadly concerning. We still think that the AI trade has legs. So we think that this is kind of not a bubble bursting, if you will. This is just kind of just some growing concerns, and adding to those concerns is just this time of the year.

"There's a lot of investors out there who are trying to kind of keep their gains for the year. So they're kind of selling now and asking questions later. So that's not really helping. So those are all things that are potentially pushing downward pressure on the equity markets. But that's been a good thing for the Treasury market in terms of that safe haven status.

"The Fed minutes came out this week and suggested that the Fed is pretty unified about higher interest rates. So we still think that that's likely going to happen. One of the things that's helping with the growth and inflation story, at least from the fixed income markets perspective, is if you think about just how much of a tailwind to economic growth the AI capex has been.

"If that slows a little bit, then potentially, economic growth slows a little bit, inflation comes down a little bit, and maybe the Fed doesn't have to hike as aggressively as what markets are pricing in. And in that scenario, that would help Treasury markets as well... It's a little bit more concerning perhaps on the economic growth side, but we don't think recession is in the cards anytime soon."

data.title: Popular Leveraged Nvidia Fund Crashes 74% From Last Month's High — WSJ
data.description:
By Jack Pitcher

Leverage cuts both ways.

One of the most popular-and until recently best performing-leveraged single-stock exchange-traded funds has crashed 74% from its Oct. 6 record, wiping out most of the fund's assets as it has tracked Nvidia's decline lower.

The GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA ETF closed 28% lower on Friday.

data.title: Brazil ex-President Bolsonaro hospitalized with abdominal pain
data.description:
Imprisoned former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro was hospitalized in Brasilia on Friday after suffering abdominal pain and distension, according to a statement from his hospital.

  • Bolsonaro, who governed from 2019 to 2022, has a history of hospitalizations and surgeries related to a stabbing in the abdomen during a 2018 campaign event

  • He will undergo exams to determine the cause of his condition, the hospital said

  • Bolsonaro was taken to the hospital after suffering "severe abdominal pain," his son Carlos Bolsonaro said earlier in the day in a post on X

  • Bolsonaro, 71, has been serving a 27-year prison sentence since last year for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to current President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva

  • The former president has been under humanitarian house arrest on medical grounds

data.title: Acuity Files 8K - Entry Into Definitive Agreement >AYI
data.description:
Acuity Inc. (AYI) filed a Form 8K - Entry Into a Definitive Agreement - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on November 20, 2026.

On November 19, 2026, Acuity Inc. ("we," "our," "us," "the Company," or similar references) entered into an Amendment No. 1 (the "Credit Facility Amendment") to that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of May 8, 2026, among the Company, the subsidiary borrowers from time to time party thereto, the various lenders from time to time party thereto, and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as administrative agent (the "Existing Credit Agreement"; the Existing Credit Agreement, as amended by the Credit Facility Amendment is referred to herein as the "Credit Agreement").

The Credit Facility Amendment, among other things, provides for an unsecured delayed draw term loan facility of up to $400 million (the "Term Loan Facility"). The Credit Agreement permits the proceeds of the Term Loan Facility to be used for general corporate purposes, including to pay a portion of the cash consideration to close the acquisition of Parameter Technologies by Acuity Intelligent Spaces US Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company (the "Acquisition"), at a later date, and to pay fees, premiums, expenses and other transaction costs incurred in connection with the Acquisition. The Term Loan Facility may be drawn in a single borrowing, subject to certain conditions, at any time through the earliest of (i) the date that is six months after the effective date of the Credit Facility Amendment, (ii) the "outside date" (as defined in the definitive acquisition agreement for the Acquisition as in effect on the signing date thereof, giving effect to any extension thereto pursuant to the terms of such definitive acquisition agreement as in effect on the signing date thereof) and (iii) the date of the termination of the Term Loan Facility commitments in accordance with the Credit Agreement. On November 19, 2026, no loans were outstanding under the Term Loan Facility.

The Term Loan Facility will mature on May 8, 2031, which is the maturity date of the revolving loans and commitments under the Existing Credit Agreement. Borrowings under the Term Loan Facility bear interest at a rate equal to an adjusted base rate or Term SOFR, plus, in each case, an applicable margin. The applicable margin is based on, at the Company's option, the Company's leverage ratio or credit rating level. Undrawn commitments under the Term Loan Facility will accrue a facility fee from and including the date that is 91 days after the effective date of the Credit Facility Amendment, which facility fee will be determined, at the Company's option, by the Company's leverage ratio or credit rating level.

The covenants and events of default that apply to the revolving loans and commitments under the Credit Agreement also apply to the Term Loan Facility, and borrowings under the Term Loan Facility are guaranteed by the subsidiaries of the Company that guarantee the revolving loans and commitments.

The foregoing summary of the Credit Facility Amendment, including the transactions contemplated thereby, does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Credit Facility Amendment, filed herewith as Exhibit 10.1 and incorporated herein by reference.

data.title: Proximity Labs Takes Strategic Stake in SVRN with 6.3% Holding
data.description:
Proximity Labs Takes Strategic Stake in SVRN with 6.3% Holding

Proximity Labs disclosed a 6.3% stake in SVRN, Inc., holding 117,647 common shares in a Schedule 13D filed Nov. 20, 2026. It acquired the shares on Oct. 28, 2025, paying nearly $3 million in NEAR tokens before SVRN's 1-for-20 reverse stock split. Its separate Series B preferred shares carry enhanced voting rights, and the group estimates it can exercise up to 9.99% of SVRN's voting power.

Investor Intent

Proximity Labs says it acquired the shares as an investment in SVRN's adoption of a NEAR-focused digital-asset treasury strategy. The group also acquired Series B preferred shares with enhanced voting rights; it says that feature could give its investment the purpose or effect of influencing SVRN's control, rather than serving solely as a passive holding.

The group will keep reviewing its investment and says it may buy or sell SVRN securities, vote its common and preferred shares, and discuss SVRN's business, strategy and governance with management, directors and other shareholders. It has not identified a specific proposal to change SVRN's operations or leadership.

Investor's Background

Proximity Labs is a Cayman Islands company that researches and develops open-source software in the NEAR Protocol ecosystem. Proximity Foundation, a Cayman Islands foundation company focused on blockchain composability and cross-chain projects, is its sole member and director. Kendall Cole and Marc Piano manage the foundation as its two directors and may share voting and investment control over Proximity Labs' SVRN holdings.
